say: GIFT SHOP AND CAFE
Right through this door. Souvenirs, coffee, and somewhere to sit.
A guestbook lies open on the front desk.
The first page is still blank.
DIRECTORY
North: Gallery One. Games Over Qualia episodes and community finds.
A bench for resting between galleries.

lines: I came in for the gift shop.
Is it through there?
Welcome!

say: A bench, angled toward the first two pieces.
A bench with a good view of the far wall.
Glass cases hold Games Over Qualia episodes. Read the front, then walk around to the back.
Paintings on the walls are community finds, with notes from guest writers.
ELEVATOR
Through this door. Up to Gallery Two, down to Storage.
STAIRS
Through this door. Fair warning: it's a bit of a walk.

lines: Wait. Why does every painting in here have a horizon?
I've read this placard three times now.
The wood frames are the community picks.
I want mine up there someday.
Evening. Don't mind me, just doing my rounds.
Funny thing about this place at night.
Sometimes the intercom crackles when nobody's touching it.
If you see a pair of eyes in the dark...
That's not me. I'd have said hello.

say: Shelves of knickknacks. A tiny ceramic frog stares back at you.
Posters for games that don't exist yet. You'd play all of them.
More knickknacks. Somebody organized these by vibe.
A shelf of snow globes. Each one has a tiny museum inside.
A poster that just says "WAIT, WHY?" in big friendly letters.
A floor lamp with a fringed shade. Very warm, very cozy.
A squeaky postcard spinner. Every card is a different game.
A basket of stickers and enamel pins. None of them are for sale. They're just vibes.
A basket of tiny plush cats. One of them looks suspiciously like the real one.
An empty cat bed. Still warm, and covered in orange fur.
A little café table. Someone left a sugar packet.
A little café table by the lamp.
Another fringed lamp. The café's favorite.
(What it says when someone looks at it.)

lines: Welcome in! Browse the racks, or come to the counter.
Coffee, tea, or cocoa? Step up to the counter.

say: A bench under the paintings.
STAIRS DOWN
Back to Gallery One, or keep going to Storage.

lines: Upstairs is so quiet.
I like it up here.
I took the stairs. Don't ask me about the stairs.

say: UP: 2F, Gallery Two. Follow the railing.
DOWN: B1, Storage.
Someone added in pencil: "AND BEYOND?"
Shelves of boxed games, labeled in three different handwritings.
A shelf of spare frames, glass panes, and one lonely controller.
A box labeled ESCORT MISSIONS.
"Fragile. Handle with patience."
A box labeled INVENTORY LIMITS.
"Some assembly required. Not all of it fits."
A box labeled UNSKIPPABLE CUTSCENES.
"Do not open. It takes forever."
A box labeled FALL DAMAGE.
"This side up. Seriously."

lines: I'm the conservator. These games came in without instructions.
I'm figuring out what they wanted to be.
The boxes over there? Abandoned mechanics.
There are no bad mechanics. Just ones that haven't found the right game yet.

say: The break table. Someone left a half-finished crossword.
The staff coffee maker. It makes one cup at a time, slowly.

pieces.title: Lantern Keeper
pieces.observation: I kept refusing to light the last lantern. Leaving one dark felt like the only choice the game let me make for myself.
pieces.intention: The last lantern is optional on purpose. Mira wanted players to notice they were allowed to stop.
pieces.hint: the one where you can choose not to light the last lantern

pieces.title: Second Breakfast
pieces.observation: The timer never ran out, but I rushed anyway. Why did a clock that never mattered make me so nervous?
pieces.intention: The clock is decoration. Tom added it late, and playtesters' panic made him keep it.
pieces.hint: the one where the clock never ran out but I still rushed

pieces.title: Tidepool
pieces.guestNote: Nothing in Tidepool tells you what to do, and somehow that made me look closer at every rock.
pieces.hint: the quiet one with the rocks and the water

pieces.title: The Long Hallway
pieces.observation: The hallway got shorter every time I walked it. I only noticed because I was bored, and the boredom was the clue.
pieces.intention: Ines shrank it a few steps each loop so the repetition itself would become the puzzle.
pieces.hint: the one with the hallway that keeps getting shorter

pieces.title: Mushroom Mail
pieces.guestNote: Delivering letters to mushrooms shouldn't feel this heavy, but every reply made me want to write back.
pieces.hint: the one where you deliver letters to mushrooms

pieces.title: Echo Quarry
pieces.observation: I mined slower than I needed to, just to hear the echo. Was the sound design quietly setting my pace?
pieces.intention: Yes. Dee tuned each echo's length so careful players would settle into a rhythm.
pieces.hint: the mining one with the echo
